etymology: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁rewh₁- ('to tear away, snatch'); cognate with Latin ruō ('to rush').
in_context: The verb indicates a failed attempt at rescue, with the negative construction (οὐδʼ... ἐρρύσατο) emphasizing that despite his desire (ἱέμενός περ), the subject could not save his companions (ἑτάρους).
